as_told.title: John Burke measures positive surface charge at stone circles

plain: This story is about the idea that ancient pyramids and stone sites give off a kind of energy that helps crops grow. A researcher, Jim Weiner, citing a book called Seed of Knowledge, Stone of Plenty, says researchers found that seeds treated at these sites increased yield per acre three to five times. Another researcher, Geoffrey Drumm, names the book's author, John Burke, and mentions Hugh Newman. Drumm says the energy was measured with electrostatic voltmeters, tools that read electric charge, and that the sites, including stone circles, showed a positive charge on the surface. He talks about the charge rather than the crops. If true, it would mean ancient builders chose or shaped these places for a practical, energetic purpose.
